**Rebuttal for Debater A: c = 1/25**

Debater B's construction does not establish its lower bound. Three independent parts V₁, V₂, V₃ have independence number n/3, not o(n). To fix this, B must add edges inside the parts, but B never checks K₅-freeness after doing so. A K₄ using two vertices from V₁ and two from V₂, together with a common neighbour in V₃, gives a K₅, and B gives no control over the internal edges that would prevent this. The claim that a Bollobás–Erdős graph has α = o(n) applies to a single graph on its own vertex set, not to the three-part union.

The pigeonhole step only analyses this one pattern. Since c must bound every admissible graph, B must show that no admissible graph exceeds n²/25 deletions. The upper bound is a bare citation ("sharp Ramsey–Turán stability") with no statement and no verification that it yields n²/18 for general K₅-free graphs with o(n) independence.

My construction is checked directly. In the C₅ blow-up, every clique lies within two consecutive parts, so the clique number is 4 once the internal graphs are triangle-free. Independence is o(n), and max-cut forces exactly n²/25 deletions. Weighted triangle-free reduced graphs, including C₇, Petersen, and Andrásfai graphs, all stay at or below 1/25. B must exhibit an admissible graph that beats n²/25, not a density pattern whose admissibility is assumed.
